The economist is Friedrich A. Hayek. The Indian monetary economist is B. R. Shenoy, whose "Note of Dissent to the Second Five Year Plan" (his minority dissent from the Panel of Economists' Memorandum underpinning India's Second Five-Year Plan Frame, 1955) drew Hayek's attention. According to Indian Liberals' summary of the "Shenoy-Hayek Correspondences, Set II" (Hoover Institution, Friedrich A. von Hayek Collection, 1959), Shenoy reported on his visit to the Oxford meeting of the Mont Pelerin Society in an October 1959 letter, Hayek replied admitting his own understanding of Indian affairs had been transformed, and a December 1959 letter signed "F.
